title: Days and dates
summary: Sequence days and months and begin recording time.
subject: maths

difficultyRamp.within: Q1 crosses a week boundary. Q2 orders days from a given start. Q3 finds preceding months. Q4 runs a timer and records seconds. Q5 reverses yesterday to find today. Q6 orders months across a year boundary. Q7 spots a five-day-week error. Q8 matches names and measured records. Q9 compares minute, hour, day and week. Q10 moves two months across a year boundary.
difficultyRamp.versus: Easy uses pictures for parts of the day, a week strip and a calendar date. Medium uses before and after across week and month boundaries. Hard works backwards from yesterday, moves two months across a year boundary and reads named time records.

questions.prompt: Today is Sunday. What day is tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Monday follows Sunday, even though it starts a new week.

narration.prompt: Today is Sunday. What day is tomorrow?

questions.prompt: Tap the days in order, starting with Thursday.
questions.explanation: Thursday and Friday come before the weekend days of Saturday and Sunday.

questions.prompt: Tap the two months just before March and June.
questions.explanation: February comes just before March. May comes just before June.

questions.prompt: Start the timer. How many seconds does Pip take?
questions.explanation: Pip takes eight seconds. The timer shows how long the turn lasts.

questions.prompt: Yesterday was Friday. What day is today?
questions.explanation: Today follows yesterday. Saturday comes after Friday.

questions.prompt: Tap the months in order, starting with November.
questions.explanation: January follows December. The months continue into a new year.

questions.prompt: Pip says a full week has only five days. Is Pip right?
questions.explanation: A full week has seven days. Five school days leave out the weekend.

questions.prompt: Tap one time for Mia and one time for Sam.
questions.explanation: Mia records four seconds and Sam records seven seconds. Each name belongs to its own record.

questions.prompt: Put these lengths of time in order, from shortest to longest.
questions.explanation: Minutes are shorter than hours. Hours are shorter than days, and seven days make one week.

questions.prompt: What month comes two months after November?
questions.explanation: December is one month after November. January is two months after November.
